memory_lessons.applicability: This parent skips complete high-bit-free words but scalar-decodes mixed blocks; the proposed mask validator tests whether avoiding that mixed-block scalar work helps.
memory_lessons.claim: The valid 64-bit ASCII-block/scalar-mixed hybrid measured 57.50 µs, slower than the 49.62 µs baseline on the supplied official timing. This does not establish that a different whole-stream mask algorithm will also regress.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a whole-stream mask candidate under the same mixed-width n=65536 protocol and retain boundary-focused correctness checks.

memory_lessons.applicability: This is a separate T1 algorithm; T2's measured result is context rather than evidence that this implementation will be faster.
memory_lessons.claim: The available T2 SIMD-prefix/scalar-suffix hybrid was valid at 39.98 µs, while T1's catalog had two distinct programs and only one valid measured result. Compare new T1 results to the same official workload without assuming the approaches compose.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare this candidate's official result with the valid T1 and T2 measurements before proposing integration.

memory_lessons.applicability: The new implementation explicitly carries expected continuation and restricted-range masks across blocks, and falls back to scalar validation for a final incomplete sequence.
memory_lessons.claim: A previous T1 whole-block bit-mask attempt ended runtime_failed without a usable timing; its observed outcome does not demonstrate either performance or a specific cause.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Use the controller's official correctness checks, especially malformed sequences crossing eight-byte boundaries and truncated suffixes.

proposal.hypothesis: A portable eight-byte bit-plane validator can check starter classes, required continuation positions, and restricted second-byte ranges across the whole stream, carrying only the few requirements that cross block boundaries. This contrasts with the selected parent, which skips ASCII blocks but scalar-decodes mixed blocks; it may reduce mixed-block scalar control flow, though the mask setup could cost more. Keep the strict scalar validator for the tail and any final sequence crossing the buffer boundary.

retained: Retained the supplied scalar UTF-8 validator as a control and fallback.
Added portable eight-byte bit-plane classification for ASCII, continuations, and valid two-, three-, and four-byte starters.
Compared continuation masks against shifted current-block starter requirements plus carried requirements from the preceding block.
Checked E0, ED, F0, and F4 second-byte restrictions, carrying lane-zero range requirements across block boundaries.
Used scalar validation for a bounded tail and for a final sequence whose continuation requirements extend beyond the processed blocks; retained the run ABI and output.

proposal.hypothesis: A portable 8-byte SWAR bit-plane classifier may reduce per-byte control flow on mixed-width inputs by classifying lead and continuation lanes together, comparing shifted continuation requirements, and checking restricted second-byte ranges. If a sequence crosses a block boundary, defer that block and suffix to the strict scalar validator instead of carrying state. This contrasts with the selected T1 parent's ASCII-block skip and the earlier carry-state variants; it is an unmeasured experiment, not a claimed speedup.

retained: Retained the strict scalar UTF-8 validator as the correctness control and bounded suffix validator.
Added portable 8-byte SWAR bit-plane extraction and lead/continuation classification without alignment assumptions or target-specific instructions.
Compared shifted continuation requirements per block and checked E0, ED, F0, and F4 second-byte restrictions.
Delegated from a block boundary to the scalar validator whenever continuation requirements cross that boundary; kept the run ABI, output, and thread budget unchanged.
